title: Campania's Metano Flip: From Above the National Average in July to 7% Below It Today
dek: Benzina and Gasolio drift slightly above the Italian average after a gentler autumn pullback, while GPL and Metano tell the real divergence story once you zoom out to the weekly data.
executive_summary: In Campania, the most recent published reading (November 2, 2026) puts self-service Benzina at €2.0386/L, Gasolio at €2.2958/L, GPL at €0.7580/kg and Metano at €1.8453/kg. Against the prior point in the tracked series (October 16), Benzina eased 1.47% and Gasolio was essentially flat at -0.01%, while GPL rose 1.99% and Metano jumped 4.02% — the sharpest move of the four. Compared with the national same-day average, Campania now runs slightly above Italy on Benzina (+0.79%) and Gasolio (+1.43%), but notably below on GPL (-3.04%) and sharply below on Metano (-7.02%). Of the region's 2,118 registered stations, 1,844 reported a price that day, an 87.1% reporting rate versus 90.4% nationally (21,645 of 23,930 stations).

Zoom out to the full weekly series tracked since the week of July 20, though, and a sharper story emerges. Benzina and Gasolio both rode the same late-summer rally as the rest of the country — up roughly 9.7% and 12.0% respectively from their summer lows to their mid-September peaks — and have since cooled in step with the national trend, with Campania's slightly gentler pullback explaining its small current premium on both. Metano and GPL are where Campania is actually diverging: the region's Metano price has climbed 21.97% since late July, ten full percentage points slower than the national 32.32% rise, which has flipped Campania from running 0.87% above the national Metano average in July to 7.02% below it today. GPL moved the opposite way, rising 6.48% in Campania since its late-August trough — almost double the national 3.63% increase — narrowing a gap that stood at -5.44% in July to just -3.04% now.

fuel_sections.heading: Benzina Holds Just Above the National Line
paragraphs: Self-service Benzina in Campania stood at €2.0386/L as of the November 2 reading, down 1.47% from the €2.0690/L recorded on October 16, the prior point in the tracked series. That puts the region a touch above the national self-service average of €2.0226/L on the same day — a premium of €0.0160/L, or 0.79%. Full-service Benzina in Campania was €2.1361/L against a €2.1633/L national full-service average, meaning full-service pricing in the region actually runs cheaper than the national figure (-1.26%) even as self-service runs slightly dearer.

The weekly series shows Benzina's Campania story closely mirrors the national one. Both climbed through late summer, with Campania up 9.78% from its week-of-July-20 average (€1.9721/L) to its week-of-September-14 peak (€2.1650/L), almost identical to the national 9.68% rise over the same stretch (€1.9756/L to €2.1669/L). Since that peak, Campania has eased 5.84% to its latest reading, a gentler retreat than the national 6.66% drop — and that smaller pullback is exactly why Campania has flipped from tracking fractionally below the national Benzina average through most of the summer to sitting slightly above it now.

fuel_sections.heading: Gasolio Stays Stickier at the Top Than the National Average
paragraphs: Campania's self-service Gasolio read €2.2958/L on November 2, essentially unchanged from the €2.2960/L recorded on October 16 (-0.01%) — the flattest move of the four fuels this period. That leaves the region €0.0323/L above the €2.2635/L national self-service average, a 1.43% premium. Full-service Gasolio was €2.4091/L in Campania against €2.4165/L nationally, a close-to-in-line -0.31%.

The weekly data explains why Campania now sits above the national Gasolio price. Both Campania and Italy as a whole rallied through late summer — Campania up 12.00% from its week-of-August-10 trough (€2.1106/L) to its week-of-September-14 peak (€2.3638/L), versus a nearly identical 12.32% national rise (€2.1133/L to €2.3736/L). But coming down off that peak, Campania has fallen just 2.88% to its latest level, while the national average has dropped 4.64% over the same span. That slower retreat is why Campania, which tracked close to the national Gasolio price all summer, now shows a visible 1.43% premium over it.

fuel_sections.heading: GPL Is Catching Up to the National Price, Fast
paragraphs: GPL self-service in Campania came in at €0.7580/kg on November 2, up 1.99% from €0.7432/kg on October 16 — the fastest day-to-day move among these two fuels this period. Even after that jump, Campania remains below the €0.7818/kg national self-service average, a gap of €0.0238/kg, or 3.04%. Full-service GPL was €0.7659/kg in the region versus €0.7906/kg nationally, a similar -3.12%.

The more striking pattern sits in the weekly trend. Campania's GPL held at a flat €0.7119/kg for most of September before climbing 6.48% to its current €0.7580/kg since the week-of-August-31 trough — nearly double the national rise of 3.63% over the same stretch (€0.7544/kg to €0.7818/kg). That faster climb has been closing a gap that was much wider earlier in the tracked period: Campania's GPL ran 5.44% below the national average in the week of July 20, and that discount has narrowed to 3.04% now. If the recent pace holds, Campania's GPL could converge with the national figure within a few weeks.

fuel_sections.heading: Metano Has Flipped From Above the National Average to Well Below It
paragraphs: Metano is Campania's biggest mover today: self-service Metano hit €1.8453/kg on November 2, up 4.02% from €1.7740/kg on October 16, the largest change among the four fuels in this reading. Yet despite that jump, Campania remains well under the €1.9847/kg national self-service average — a gap of €0.1394/kg, or 7.02%. Full-service Metano was €1.9406/kg in the region against a €2.0519/kg national figure, a comparable -5.42% discount.

This is the most interesting trend in today's data. Metano has risen every week in the tracked series, both in Campania and nationally, but at very different speeds: Campania is up 21.97% since the week of July 20 (€1.5129/kg to €1.8453/kg), while the national average has risen 32.32% over the identical stretch (€1.4999/kg to €1.9847/kg). Those growth rates point the same direction but differ sharply in scale, and the cumulative effect is a full reversal: in the week of July 20, Campania's Metano price was actually 0.87% above the national average; today it sits 7.02% below it. No other fuel in this dataset has flipped sides of the national average this dramatically over the weeks tracked so far.

network_section.heading: 1,844 of 2,118 Registered Stations Reported Today
paragraphs: Campania had 2,118 registered fuel stations as of the November 2 reading, of which 1,844 actively reported prices — a reporting rate of 87.1%. That's below the national reporting rate of 90.4% (21,645 of 23,930 registered stations reporting nationwide), though it is in line with where Campania has sat all season: the region's reporting rate was 87.6% back on July 21 (1,853 of 2,117 stations), meaning it has moved in a narrow, stable band for over three months.

A reporting rate below 90% means roughly one in eight registered Campania stations did not submit a price on the day captured here — a normal, structural feature of MIMIT's self-reported price network rather than a sign of regional stations closing, since the registered count itself has barely moved (2,117 to 2,118) over the same period. It does mean the regional averages above are drawn from the subset of stations that report consistently, which is the best available signal but not a full census of every pump in Campania.

methodology_section.heading: Built by an Unattended Pipeline, Not a Spreadsheet
paragraphs: Everything in this report — the price and station data, the week-by-week trend analysis for each of the four fuels, the choice of Campania as today's featured region, and the prose above — is produced automatically, once a day, by a pipeline built with Claude Code. A scheduled task pulls MIMIT's registry and price feeds, recomputes the national and regional averages, selects the day's region on a deterministic alphabetical rotation through Italy's 20 regions, and has an AI agent read the resulting numbers and write the analysis directly from them — no templated placeholders, no hand-typed figures.

That stands in contrast to how a project like this is traditionally run: a person manually downloading a CSV, pasting numbers into a spreadsheet, recalculating a few averages by hand, and writing a summary paragraph whenever they find the time — a process that doesn't scale past a handful of regions and tends to lapse the first time life gets busy. The pipeline behind Fuel Dashboard runs the same checks every day regardless, which is also why the region rotation is visible and auditable rather than cherry-picked: Campania was today's subject because the calendar put it there, not because of anything newsworthy happening in the region specifically.

closing.heading: Explore Beyond Campania
paragraphs: The live Fuel Dashboard at https://adeo-blip.github.io/fuel-price-italy/ opens by default on Agip Eni's brand-level view, but that's just one way to slice the same underlying data. Use the scope picker to switch to Region to compare Campania against any of Italy's other 19 regions, to Province or Municipality for a more local look, or to another Operator/Brand to see how a specific fuel network is pricing relative to the market — the same four fuels and the same weekly trends covered in this report, from whichever angle you want to look at them.

pull_quote: Campania's Metano price has flipped from 0.87% above the national average in July to 7.02% below it today — even as the fuel itself rose over 20% regionally and over 30% nationally this autumn.
caption:
Today's Fuel Dashboard spotlight is on Campania — and the most interesting number isn't the headline price, it's a reversal hiding in the weekly trend.

Back in July, Campania's Metano price was running slightly above the Italian national average. Today, after Metano prices climbed more than 20% in the region and over 30% nationally this autumn, Campania sits 7% below the national average instead. Benzina and Gasolio are drifting the other way, sitting just slightly above the national line after a gentler post-peak pullback than the rest of the country. And GPL is the fuel to watch next: Campania's GPL has risen almost twice as fast as the national average in recent weeks, closing a gap that was over 5% wide in July down to about 3% now.

None of this is hand-typed. Fuel Dashboard is a self-updating dashboard and daily report that pulls Italy's official MIMIT fuel price feed every morning, recomputes national and regional averages across all 20 regions and four fuel types, picks a new region to spotlight on a fixed rotation, and has an AI agent (Claude Code) write the trend analysis above straight from the numbers, no templates involved. It does the job a manually-maintained Excel sheet would do, except it runs every single day without anyone needing to remember to open it.

Full interactive dashboard, region comparisons, and today's full report: https://adeo-blip.github.io/fuel-price-italy/
